newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Fischler says EU wheat export tax may soon be cut.
newsitem.headline: Fischler says EU wheat export tax may soon be cut.

text.p: European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said a tax on daily wheat exports could soon be cut following a fall prices.

Asked at a three-day informal meeting of EU farm ministers whether the tax would be changed, Fischler told Reuters, "Yes, we did the same also in the past. We lowered the taxes when prices went down and we raised taxes when prices went up."
Asked whether it would be sooner or later, Fischler, said, "I would say sooner."
The EU on May 14 imposed taxes of 15 ecus a tonne on daily exports of soft wheat grain and 20 ecus a tonne on wheat flour to stop prices overheating.
But world wheat prices had in the last two weeks fallen about 10 ecus a tonne, Fischler said, adding that the tax was very flexible.
"It depends on development in the world market price. nothing else. It's not in our interest to block exports but it's in our interest to have enough grain in the EU so as to reach the next harvest."
Fischler confirmed that the EU was still using U.S. soft red winter prices as a benchmark for wheat exports and denied reports of a switch to U.S. hard red winter prices.
"It was a misunderstanding...We are doing the same as a year ago...There's no change in policy," he said.
The tax was a precautionary move after concern about low stocks and this year's harvest following a prolonged spell of dry weather had driven prices sharply higher.
It effectively ended EU wheat exports for 1996/97 (July/June) as an alternative weekly wheat export tender had earlier been closed.
